**What type of PR is this?**
/kind flake
/sig cli
/area kubectl

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

A race condition could occur where the two calls to `kubectl logs` in the `[sig-cli] Kubectl client Kubectl logs should be able to retrieve and filter logs [Conformance]` e2e test would not have enough logs generated between them.

This PR adds a delay between test calls to `kubectl logs` to ensure that enough logs have been generated.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #92468 

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
NONE
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

```docs

```

@eddiezane @soltysh Looks like there are actually two problems here. The initial failure mentioned in this issue was because tailing one line is returning two [example](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-kind-ipv6-e2e-parallel/1293148191239180289), but there is also the issue of there not being older logs (mentioned above), which @eddiezane is addressing in #93763
/retitle [Flaky Test] [sig-cli] Kubectl client Kubectl logs should be able to retrieve and filter logs [Conformance]

- Tailing one line is returning two
It's because the `--tail` flag will result in finding the start line:
```
	// Search start point based on tail line.
	start, err := tail.FindTailLineStartIndex(f, opts.tail)
```
So when reading the log while writing continuously. The start index will not be the actually `--tail` number.

- Issue of there not being older logs
It's because the pod `agnhos` will be restarted after 20s. If `recent logs` is the old pod and the `older logs` is the new pod. There's no comparability between them.

Still flaking as of the 24th: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-conformance-kind-ga-only/1309146359319760896

review_comments:
@hasheddan this whole test is confusing.

```
gomega.Expect(recent).To(gomega.BeNumerically("<", older), "expected recent(%v) to be less than older(%v)\nrecent lines:\n%v\nolder lines:\n%v\n", recent, older, recentOut, olderOut)
```

I believe it's asserting that there are less `recent` (logs created 1 second ago `--since=1s`) than there are `older` (logs created 24 hours ago `--since=24h`). Which should be the case. The flake was occurring when there isn't enough time between the `recent` and `older` (because they are both basically starting from 0 logs).

Thoughts?

Hmm shouldn't the first wait (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93763/files#diff-fde2ce0a73639d19347a5ea6fe001ba6R1481) take care of making it true that there are more logs in the last 24h than in the last 1s? This is why this flake is concerning to me because it _seems_ like the test logic is sound. If anything, it looks like we should bump the first wait to a longer period.

@hasheddan I _think_ that the test starts with 0 logs (the pod is spun up at the very start of this test) so that initial wait doesn't create more `older` logs. The test failures looked like they were because the two vars were equal at a very low number (like 5).

@eddiezane I believe the purpose of the first wait is to make there be older logs than 1s. So if the pod starts up and starts producing logs, then we wait 2.5 seconds, if any logs are produced in the first 1.5 seconds they should be in `older` but not in `recent`. Therefore, extending the first wait would increase the likelihood that logs are produced before the last `1s` that `recent` looks at.
